what: Tempus AI sequences tumours and builds a library of the results. It sells the diagnostic tests to oncologists, and sells the resulting de-identified data to pharmaceutical companies developing cancer drugs.
customers: Oncologists ordering genomic tests, and pharmaceutical companies buying clinical and molecular data.
money: de-identified clinical data licensed to drug developers
moat: A dataset linking genomic results to what happened to the patient afterwards, which grows every time a test is run and which cannot be bought from anyone else.
risks: A $189M net loss and negative free cash flow: the business does not yet fund itself
Reimbursement for genomic tests is set by Medicare and insurers and is not guaranteed
7.2 times sales for a company still proving the model
opportunities: Revenue grew from $321M to $1.3B in three years and is $1.5B over the last twelve months
Analysts see about 50% upside, with 18 covering the stock, and the data business carries far higher margins than testing
watch: Data and services revenue growth, and the path to positive cash flow.
